items.title: How Airport Baggage Systems Actually Work
items.content_text: A bag travels kilometres underground, is screened by CT, and is tracked by radio tag. Most bags that go missing are simply late, and connections cause most of it.

items.title: How Recycling Actually Works
items.content_text: Aluminium recycles indefinitely and profitably, most plastic does neither, and one wrong item can ruin a whole batch. The difference is chemistry, not effort.

items.title: How Electricity Grids Stay Balanced
items.content_text: Electricity is produced and consumed in the same instant, the whole system runs on almost no stored energy, and frequency is the signal that keeps it from collapsing.

items.title: How Clinical Trials Actually Work
items.content_text: Most drugs that reach human testing still fail, blinding matters more than sample size, and the biggest problem is trials that were never published. Here's the actual machinery.

items.title: How Satellite Navigation Actually Works
items.content_text: Satellites don't know where you are and receive nothing from you. The system is a clock broadcast, which is why relativity matters and why your phone knows time atomically.

items.title: How Wildfires Actually Spread
items.content_text: Wood does not burn, fires create their own weather, and most houses are lost to embers rather than flames. Here's the mechanism behind fire behaviour and why suppression backfired.

items.title: How Refrigeration Changed What We Eat
items.content_text: Cooling does not kill anything, its first refrigerants were poisonous, and its replacements damaged the ozone layer. Here's the technology the entire food system now depends on.

items.title: How Noise-Cancelling Headphones Work
items.content_text: Cancellation works brilliantly on engine rumble and barely at all on speech, and the reason is physics rather than product quality. Here's what actually determines performance.

items.title: How Sunscreen Actually Works
items.content_text: SPF is not a time multiplier, most people apply a quarter of the tested amount, and the number says nothing about the radiation that ages skin. Here's the real chemistry.

items.title: How Banks Actually Create Money
items.content_text: Banks do not lend out deposits. They create new money when they lend, which is the opposite of what most people are taught. Here's how it genuinely works.

items.title: How Dental Cavities Actually Form
items.content_text: Cavities are not caused by sugar directly but by acid from bacteria feeding on it. Here's the chemistry, why frequency matters more than quantity, and what actually prevents them.

items.title: How Laser Vision Correction Actually Works
items.content_text: Reshaping the cornea with a laser can eliminate the need for glasses. Here's the optics behind it, what the procedures actually involve, and the genuine limits.

items.title: How Motivation Actually Works
items.content_text: Waiting to feel motivated is the most common productivity mistake. Here's what the research says about where motivation comes from and why action usually precedes it.

items.title: How Passports Came to Exist
items.content_text: For most of history you could cross borders without documents. Here's how the passport became universal, why photographs were resisted, and what the power gap means now.

items.title: How Shipping Containers Changed Global Trade
items.content_text: A plain steel box reorganised the world economy more thoroughly than most technologies. Here's why standardisation mattered more than the box itself.

items.title: How Smartphone Chips Are Actually Designed and Manufactured
items.content_text: Behind every new phone launch is a multi-year chip design cycle spanning architecture, fabrication, and packaging. Here's how a smartphone chip actually gets made.

items.title: How Supermarkets Actually Make Money
items.content_text: Grocery margins are among the thinnest in retail, which is why the profit comes from supplier payments, own-brand products and cash flow rather than from selling food.

items.title: How Drinking Water Treatment Actually Works
items.content_text: Chlorination saved more lives than most medicines, and the pipe matters more than the plant. Here's what treatment actually removes, and what it was never designed to.

items.title: Why Time Zones Exist and Who Decides Them
items.content_text: Time zones were invented by railways, not governments, and their boundaries are political rather than astronomical. Here's who actually sets them and why they keep changing.

items.title: How Elevators Actually Work
items.content_text: Elevators are counterweighted, cannot free-fall, and are dispatched by algorithms solving a genuinely hard problem. The invention that made skyscrapers possible was the brake.
